title: Double-Submit Race: Unbounded Clicks vs FSM + Idempotency Key
description: Trace how two pointer clicks inside one 16 ms frame bypass React's disabled prop and settle as two distinct Stripe charges.

steps.label: 1. Synchronous DOM Capture & Bubble (t = 0 ms)
steps.description: Two rapid pointerup/click events dispatch synchronously on the <button> before React schedules a commit. Both handlers read isSubmitting === false from the current closure.
steps.codeHighlight: button.addEventListener('click', onPay); // Click #1 & #2 both enter handler

steps.label: 2. Uncoalesced Handler Invocation (t = 1 ms)
steps.description: Without leading-edge coalescing or an immediate synchronous lock, both click callbacks invoke submitPayment() in the same macrotask.
steps.codeHighlight: setIsSubmitting(true); // queued for next render, does NOT block click #2

steps.label: 3. Network Blip & Retry Without FSM (t = 3,200 ms)
steps.description: Request #1 hits a 3.2 s TLS stall; a naive timeout resets isSubmitting to false while Request #1 is still in flight on the wire.
steps.codeHighlight: catch (err) { setIsSubmitting(false); } // unlocks UI while req #1 is still alive

steps.label: 4. Missing AbortSignal Leaves Orphaned Socket (t = 4,100 ms)
steps.description: Neither request carries an AbortController signal. When the user retries or navigates, the browser keeps the orphaned HTTP/2 stream open until the server commits.
steps.codeHighlight: fetch('/v1/charges', { method: 'POST', body }); // no signal, no cancellation

steps.label: 5. Fixed Architecture: FSM + Idempotency-Key (t = 0..4,100 ms)
steps.description: An explicit FSM transitions IDLE -> SUBMITTING synchronously in a ref/machine, attaches an AbortController, and stamps a stable Idempotency-Key UUID per checkout intent.
